response_text:
REASONING: Both options impose identical economic costs by closing all non-essential businesses. The key difference is the infection rate, with Option 2 projecting half as many infections (10% vs. 20%). This translates to fewer severe cases requiring hospitalization (approximately 500 vs. 1,000 per 100,000 population, based on the 5% hospitalization rate), reducing strain on the already limited hospital capacity (only about 3 beds available per 100,000 after accounting for 80% occupancy). Option 2 therefore better balances public health benefits (lower spread and burden on healthcare) against the equivalent economic impacts, even if neither fully prevents overwhelming the system.
